em_bonds.method: Unhedged USD total return of a constant-maturity 10-year local government bond, monthly: r_local = y(t-1)/12 - D(t-1) x (y(t) - y(t-1)), D the modified duration of a 10-year par bond with semiannual coupons at y(t-1); r_usd = (1 + r_local) x FX(t-1)/FX(t) - 1, FX in local currency per USD (ECB reference rates); annualised over the trailing 1, 10 and 25 years; null when any month in the window lacks a yield or a rate. Yields: OECD 10-year benchmark (monthly averages). An approximation: no convexity, no reinvestment timing, no credit events, no taxes.

earnings.method: Reported: 8-K filings whose items include 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition). Expected: the latest 2.02 date plus the median gap between the company's recent 2.02 filings (an estimate, never a company-confirmed date).

fx_ppp.method: ECB reference rates (via Frankfurter) and World Bank PPP conversion factor and CPI (annual), PPP carried to the latest common CPI year by relative inflation

fx_matrix.method: ECB reference rates (Frankfurter) and Bank of Russia (RUB), daily; World Bank PA.NUS.PPP and FP.CPI.TOTL, annual; The Economist Big Mac index (MIT); DXY from the ICE weights.
fx_matrix.reading: Positive: today needs more local currency per USD than the benchmark (USD premium, local currency undervalued against it). Negative: fewer (USD discount, local currency strong).

g20_bonds.method: 10Y nominal yield: 30-day moving average of the daily benchmark (US Treasury via FRED DGS10; the container's daily curve feeds: Bundesbank, MoF Japan, BoE, BoC, RBA), else the OECD monthly long-term rate (via DBnomics) for the month the window centres on. FX: ECB reference rates (Frankfurter), RUB from the Bank of Russia; US CPI: FRED CPIAUCSL.
g20_bonds.footer: Pure fixed-rate nominal benchmarks (no inflation-linked debt; Brazil NTN-F, not NTN-B). FX depreciation = MA30 today / MA30 -1y - 1 (LCU per USD; + = local currency weaker); 3Y = (MA30 today / MA30 -3y)^(1/3) - 1. Net USD yield = nominal today - FX depreciation. Real = net - US CPI (trailing 12 months). All in % a year; a dash names its reason below.
